answer: Twice a day the cellar master reads the thermometer and writes the figure in the cellar log, so the wine ages at the temperature the book proves. A nebula log filled in from memory fails at once: the master checks the reading against the ember thermometer itself, and a figure copied from yesterday matches no instrument at all. Faking a year of cellar records means bribing the master, forging seven hundred entries and paying 14,700, while the nectar page in the log is read at every racking, so a cellar whose temperature was never recorded is emptied by the estate.
